permissive.label: Anyone can use it, freely

yamlDiff.originalPlaceholder: Paste or drop the original YAML (or JSON)
yamlDiff.changedPlaceholder: Paste or drop the changed YAML (or JSON)
yamlDiff.idle: Fill both panes and the comparison runs as you type.
yamlDiff.privacy: Both documents are parsed and compared in this browser — nothing is uploaded, which is the point for manifests carrying hostnames and secret names.
yamlDiff.resolveAnchors: Resolve anchors and aliases to their values
yamlDiff.parseFailed: One side did not parse — nothing was compared
yamlDiff.equivalent: No differences — the two documents resolve to the same structure
yamlDiff.equivalentStructural: Same resolved structure · {n} formatting or anchor differences
yamlDiff.documentCountMismatch: Document count differs: {original} vs {changed} — documents were paired in order and the extras reported whole

rule.keyOrder: Mapping key order, quoting and indentation are ignored; sequence order is compared, because a list's order carries meaning.
rule.anchors: Aliases are resolved to their values, so an edit behind a shared anchor shows at every alias site; an anchor or alias that changed with the value intact is reported separately as structural.
rule.mergeKeys: Merge keys (<<) are expanded before comparing, and a node's own keys win over merged ones.
rule.types: Type is part of the value: 8080, "8080" and !!str 8080 are reported as type changes, not as a generic change.
rule.sequences: Sequences of mappings pair by name, id or key when that field is unique on both sides, so one inserted item does not cascade; a reorder is still reported.
rule.blockScalars: Block scalars compare by resolved string, so the trailing newline that |- strips is a real change; a restyle with the same value is structural.
rule.comments: Comments are not part of the YAML data model and are not compared.
rule.multiDoc: --- streams pair document by document; a count mismatch is reported instead of comparing only the first.
rule.duplicateKeys: A duplicate mapping key in the input uses the last occurrence and is reported as a warning.

note.raw-text-mode: Raw-text mode compares characters, not structure: key order, quoting and indentation all count.
note.parse-error: One side did not parse, so nothing was compared.
note.document-count-mismatch: The two sides hold a different number of --- documents; documents were paired in order and the extras reported whole.
note.merge-keys-expanded: Merge keys (<<) were expanded before comparing.
note.anchors-unresolved: Aliases were compared as *name references, not as their resolved values.
note.yaml11-ambiguous-scalars: Unquoted y/n/yes/no/on/off read as strings here (YAML 1.2 Core) and as booleans under YAML 1.1 — quote them if a boolean was meant.
note.sequence-matched-by-identity: Sequences of mappings were paired by an identity field instead of by position.
note.duplicate-keys: A mapping declares the same key twice; the last occurrence was used.
note.truncated: Only the first 2000 changes are listed.

retryBackoff.factorHint: Multiplier applied per retry. Must be greater than 1.
retryBackoff.incrementHint: Milliseconds added to the delay on every retry.
retryBackoff.maxDelayHint: Leave empty for no cap. Once the cap is reached, every later delay stays flat at it.
retryBackoff.excludeInitial: Max attempts excludes the initial request
retryBackoff.excludeInitialNote: On: the number above counts retries only, the initial request is extra. Off: it counts every attempt, initial request included.

jitter.full: Full — anywhere from zero to the delay

retryBackoff.callerTimeoutHint: Optional. Leave empty to skip the budget check.
retryBackoff.emptyHint: Fix the highlighted field to see the schedule.
retryBackoff.note: Computed from the policy alone — nothing is sent to any upstream service. Jitter is reported as the range a real client falls inside, never as one sampled draw.
retryBackoff.headlineRange: {attempts} attempts, {expected} of waiting on average, up to {max} in the worst case.
retryBackoff.finalDelay: The last wait, before attempt {attempt}, is {delay}.
retryBackoff.noRetries: This budget allows one attempt and no retry, so there is nothing to wait for.
retryBackoff.retryCount: {count, plural, =0 {no retries} one {# retry} other {# retries}}
retryBackoff.capFlattened: Cap reached at attempt {attempt} — every later delay stays at {delay}.
retryBackoff.timeoutExceeded: Worst case waits {wait}, which overruns your {timeout} budget.
retryBackoff.timeoutOk: Worst case waits {wait}, inside your {timeout} budget.

formula.none: Delays are exact — no jitter applied.
formula.equal: Equal jitter: half the delay is fixed, the other half is drawn uniformly, so each wait lands between half the delay and the full delay.
formula.full: Full jitter: the wait is drawn uniformly between zero and the computed delay.

retryBackoff.errInitialDelay: Initial delay must be a whole number of milliseconds, at least 1.
retryBackoff.errFactor: Factor must be greater than 1 and at most 100. A factor of 1 is the fixed strategy.
retryBackoff.errIncrement: Increment must be a whole number of milliseconds, 0 or more.
retryBackoff.errMaxDelay: Cap must be a whole number of milliseconds, at least 1.
retryBackoff.errCapBelowInitial: Cap must be at least the initial delay.
retryBackoff.errMaxAttempts: Attempts must be a whole number from 1 to 100.
retryBackoff.errCallerTimeout: Timeout must be a whole number of milliseconds, at least 1.

csvColumns.note: Runs on the text you paste. Drop, then rename, then reorder — in that fixed order, always against the original header.
csvColumns.raggedCount: {n}{more} rows don't match the header width
csvColumns.previewTruncated: Showing the first {shown} of {total} lines. Copy or download for the whole file.
csvColumns.raggedListLabel: Rows that don't match the header width
csvColumns.unusedRenames: Rename ignored — these columns are not in the output: {names}

imageRotateFlip.drop: Drop an image, or click to browse
imageRotateFlip.privacy: The file is sent to the Forge API for the transform and is never stored.
imageRotateFlip.tooLarge: That image is larger than {mb} MB.
imageRotateFlip.fitNote: Off a quarter turn the rotated image no longer fits its old frame: expand keeps every pixel, crop keeps the original size and cuts the corners, fit scales the whole thing down.
imageRotateFlip.idle: Drop an image to see it reoriented.
imageRotateFlip.badgeSnapped: Snapped to the exact quarter turn
imageRotateFlip.badgeReencode: Geometry is exact; the codec re-encodes
imageRotateFlip.note: Rotations of 90°, 180° and 270° move pixels without blending them. Any other angle resamples. Animated GIF, APNG and animated WebP are not supported yet.

exifStrip.drop: Drop a JPEG, PNG or WebP to strip its metadata
exifStrip.privacy: Processed on our servers and never stored. Up to {mb} MB per image.
exifStrip.idle: Removed: GPS, capture time, camera and device info, embedded thumbnail, editing history. Kept: orientation, colour profile, dimensions, pixel data.
exifStrip.note: Still images only. Video, PDF, HEIC, AVIF and GIF are out of scope, and C2PA provenance manifests are left intact.
exifStrip.verdictClean: This file carries no removable metadata
exifStrip.strippedCaveat: The image itself is unchanged — same pixels, same dimensions, nothing re-encoded.
exifStrip.cleanCaveat: Returned byte for byte as it arrived.
exifStrip.detailNothing: Nothing was removed from this file.
exifStrip.detailOrientation: Exif orientation {value} was read from the file and carried across.
exifStrip.detailNoOrientation: The file declared no Exif orientation, so display is unaffected.
exifStrip.summaryStripped: Removed {fields} metadata fields ({families}), {kb} KB. Image otherwise unchanged.
exifStrip.summaryClean: No removable metadata found. File returned unchanged.

validate.luhnCaveat: Luhn pass only checks digit structure — not that the card exists or has funds.
